messages:
Maya: Quick design review — proposing a compact latency row for the service detail page. Idea: tiny sparkline for throughput on the left, p95 band overlay on the main sparkline, and a lightweight granularity slider instead of the current dropdown. Thoughts?

Kevin: Love the sparkline idea. Is the p95 band a filled area or two lines? filled area would be easier to scan at a glance. :+1:

Anya: Fill sounds good, but accessibility: filled areas with subtle color differences can be hard to read for low-vision users. We should add a pattern or dashed boundary option for high-contrast mode.

Olivia: Agree re: contrast. Also bringing up keyboard nav — can users tab into the granularity slider and adjust with arrow keys? Current slider is mouse-only.

Maya: Yes, keyboard support planned. UX detail: slider steps -> auto, 1s, 5s, 10s, 1m. Default auto picks bucket size based on time range.

Sam: One thing I worry about: sampling explanation. People hit the sampling toggle and are confused why p95 jumps. Can we add an inline microcopy and a tooltip example showing sampled vs unsampled behavior?

Kevin: Microcopy suggestion: "Sampling reduces query volume — p95 may vary when sampling is enabled. Use 100% for exact baselines." Short and to the point.

Anya: For the tooltip, show a tiny table: 100% vs 10% sampling with example counts. Maybe include a link to docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/observability/sampling?utm=slack-review

Maya: Draft tooltip content: ```Sampling: We sample raw traces to reduce cost. Lower sampling reduces query fidelity; use 100% for audits. Example: 10k requests -> sampled 1k (10%).```

Olivia: Nice. Also: heatmap bucket labels — current UX shows bucket midpoints (e.g., "250ms"). Product asked for ranges (e.g., "200–300ms") to be more interpretable. Which do we prefer?

Sam: Ranges are clearer for non-technical users. Midpoints are compact but confusing. Ranges + aria-labels for screen readers (e.g., "200 to 300 milliseconds: 12 samples")

Kevin: Small visual request — when hovering a p95 spike, show a tiny inline card with route breakdown (top 3 routes contributing to spike). That helps root-cause quickly.

Maya: Love the route breakdown idea. But keep it lightweight: top 3 routes only, no giant table. Maybe an affordance to open the full route panel.

Anya: Accessibility nit on tooltips: ensure they are reachable by keyboard and use role="dialog" or aria-describedby patterns so screen readers announce them. Also ensure tooltip text size meets 14px minimum in the new CSS variables.

Maya: Noted. Implementation note from infra: observability-bot says capacity for live tail queries is limited; if we surface per-route breakdown on hover we should use cached aggregates to avoid live fanout. observability-bot: "Use precomputed top-k per timebucket; avoid realtime fanout for hover cards."

Sam: UX copy for granularity: change label from "Resolution" to "Granularity"? Product prefers "Resolution" but I think "Granularity" maps better to developer mental model.

Kevin: I'm fine with "Granularity" as long as the tooltip clarifies: "How data is bucketed across the time range."

Olivia: One more: color palette — we currently use green->red for heatmaps. For colorblind users, please provide a second palette (blue->purple) and a high-contrast toggle. Also include a legend with numeric ranges, not just a color bar.

Maya: Proposal summary (for the ticket):
- Compact left sparkline for throughput + main sparkline with p95 filled band
- Granularity slider (keyboard accessible) with auto heuristics
- Sampling toggle with inline microcopy + example tooltip + link to docs
- Heatmap bucket labels as ranges + aria-labels
- Hover card for p95 spikes showing cached top-3 route breakdowns
- Alternate color palettes and an explicit legend with numeric ranges
- Accessibility: keyboard tooltips, 14px min text, pattern/fill for p95 band in high-contrast mode

Anya: Looks solid. Can we also add acceptance criteria for a11y: pass axe rules for contrast and keyboard, and include a VO walkthrough?

Maya: Added to ticket. I'll file mockups and a11y checklist. Thanks all — will post initial Figma and prototype link soon. :rocket:

observability-bot: "Deployed design-checker: please attach Figma link and tag @design for review. Reminder: include sample data set for QA."

Kevin: Quick follow-up — should the mini throughput sparkline be tappable on mobile to expand into a full timechart? Mobile product asked for that.

Maya: Yes, tap-to-expand on mobile. Add to prototype notes.
